features.summary: FusionMultiSelect, the reference slice (D17.8): one declaration of the Syncfusion MultiSelect by its JavaScript names, value, dataSource, dataBind, showPopup, hidePopup, change and filtering, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of change and filtering; the input it is, its value committed by change; and the render helpers that render it bound to a model member and name its fields. Main spreads the slice over seven files whose events, writes and calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline, and a Reactive extension on the vendor's builder; the redesign declares it in one file, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its value typed nullable as the vendor holds it and its data named as every framework read names it (M21.D1).

sentences.text: public Property<IEnumerable<TItem>> Items<TItem>() where TItem : class => Property<IEnumerable<TItem>>("dataSource");
internal static string Of(MemberInfo member) => member.GetCustomAttribute<JsonPropertyNameAttribute>()?.Name ?? Of(member.Name);

FusionMultiSelect declares value as Property<string[]?>, since EJ2's value holds null until a choice, so Value.Set(null) clears the selection as main's SetValue(null) does; dataSource as Items<TItem>(); dataBind, showPopup and hidePopup as methods; and change and filtering as events whose payload is the listener's first argument.
Change's payload reads value and isInteracted; Filtering's reads text, writes preventDefaultAction, and calls updateData with any source of a list, a response body's among them.
A FusionMultiSelect bound to a member is an input: its Value, committed by Change, is what a form sends and a check reads.

field.FusionMultiSelect(build => ..) renders the element under the field's id and binding name, starting at the member's value as M21.D1 writes it; field.FusionMultiSelect(items, build => ..) hands EJ2 the items the same way; and Fields<TItem>(text, value) and Fields<TItem>(text, value, groupBy) name each field as every framework read names it.

The rendered FusionMultiSelect's Reactive(m => m.Change, pipeline) and Reactive(m => m.Filtering, pipeline) handle its events from the plan's start; p.Component<FusionMultiSelect>(m => m.Allergies) reaches it in any block.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's MultiSelect as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-dropdowns/src/multi-select/multi-select.d.ts, its FilteringEventArgs in src/drop-down-base/drop-down-base.d.ts, dataBind in @syncfusion/ej2-base/src/component.d.ts), checked member by member by scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py; its ASP.NET Core builder as the probes render it (fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults, fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json); and the browser.

defects.defect: The redesign declares Value as Property<string[]> (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionMultiSelect/FusionMultiSelect.cs:19 at 65fdf118d) where EJ2's value is number[] | string[] | boolean[] | object[] | null, null by default (@syncfusion/ej2-dropdowns/src/multi-select/multi-select.d.ts:416), so an untouched box types as a list and main's clear, SetValue(null) (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionMultiSelect/FusionMultiSelectExtensions.cs:36-41 at 623dd4a27), is a nullable warning: the vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) refuses the nullability by ALIS019, and the rewrite declares Property<string[]?>.

A text field named by a member that carries [JsonPropertyName("label")] shows no text: in the redesign the field names label (Alis.Reactive/Members/JsonMemberName.cs:11 at 65fdf118d) while EJ2 writes the data handed over with the view through Newtonsoft as displayLabel (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults); in main the field names displayLabel, the camel case of the C# name (Alis.Reactive/PlanAuthoring/ExpressionPaths/JsonMemberName.cs:9 at 623dd4a27), while an endpoint's body, written by System.Text.Json, holds label. The rewrite names the field and writes the handed data by one writer (M21.D1, probe:fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json).

promises.page: An intake page whose allergy FusionMultiSelect is rendered with the items Penicillin and Latex handed over with the view, of an allergy class whose display label member carries [JsonPropertyName("label")], and Fields(a => a.DisplayLabel, a => a.AllergyCode).
promises.gesture: Click the allergy box to open its list.
promises.outcome: The list shows Penicillin and Latex.
promises.opposite: Choosing Latex shows Latex in the box, and the form sends its code 9.
promises.defect: EJ2 writes the handed items through Newtonsoft as displayLabel while the field names label, so the list shows two empty options.

promises.page: An intake page whose Load allergies button requests the ward's allergies, which the endpoint writes as label and allergyCode, and sets them as the FusionMultiSelect's items, with Fields(a => a.DisplayLabel, a => a.AllergyCode) on the same allergy class.
promises.gesture: Click Load allergies, then click the allergy box to open its list.
promises.outcome: The list shows Penicillin and Latex.
promises.opposite: Before Load allergies is clicked, the list shows no options.
promises.defect: The field names displayLabel, the camel case of the C# name, while the body holds label, so the list shows two empty options, as main names fields.

Main's payload is a C# class whose setter no view runs in the browser; a member the vendor reads back from its listener is the payload's declared Property.

features.summary: The package: FusionComponent, the base of every Fusion declaration, which carries Syncfusion's vendor as data, its object at ej2_instances.0 on the element and its events heard by addEventListener and removeEventListener, so the one driver follows it as it follows an app's vendor; and the writing every Fusion render helper uses for the C# values it hands EJ2 (M21.D1), by which AddReactiveFusion, a registration that only sets Newtonsoft's process-wide default to camel case on both lines, leaves. Main names its vendor by the string fusion, which its runtime picks a driver by.

sentences.text: public sealed override ComponentVendor Vendor => FusionVendor;
public static IServiceCollection AddReactiveFusion(this IServiceCollection services)

FusionComponent.FusionVendor is ComponentVendor.Define("fusion", objectPath: "ej2_instances.0", subscribe: "addEventListener", unsubscribe: "removeEventListener"), and each Fusion event declares its payload as the listener's first argument.

A Fusion render helper hands EJ2 the component's starting value and the items the view gives it as a JRaw of the text field.ValueJson and field.Json(options) write, so EJ2 writes them with the names and escapes the plan's own writer gives.
No Fusion door writes a Newtonsoft setting: an app's own JsonConvert calls keep the app's settings, and AddReactiveFusion leaves.

meanings.meaning: A Fusion render helper gives EJ2 each C# value it writes into the component's options, its starting value and the items the view hands it, as a Newtonsoft JRaw of the text the plan's one literal writer writes (D17.13, N17.10, D7.7), under the app's System.Text.Json options and escaped as M19.D3 escapes the plan, so the data names each member as every framework read names it (D2.9); EJ2 writes a JRaw as its text (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json). The vendor builder's own DataSource(object), reached through the build callback, stays the vendor's, named by the app's own Newtonsoft settings, since EJ2 writes C# data through JsonConvert.DefaultSettings (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults); no Fusion door writes a Newtonsoft setting, and AddReactiveFusion, which only set that default to camel case for the whole process, leaves.

features.oracle: Syncfusion.EJ2.AspNet.Core 33.1.47's builder and ScriptManager as ASP.NET Core 10 MVC renders them (spec/probes/AspNetCoreBinding/FusionProbes.cs: fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults, fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json, fusion-ej2-script-text-escaped); Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3's JsonConvert.DefaultSettings, process-wide by its type; EJ2 33.1.47's Component base as @syncfusion/ej2-base declares it; and the browser.

defects.defect: AddReactiveFusion sets Newtonsoft's JsonConvert.DefaultSettings to camel case for the whole process on both lines (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/ReactiveFusionServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:67 at 623dd4a27, :63 at 65fdf118d), so every JsonConvert call the app makes without settings of its own writes camel case names, a choice the app never made. The rewrite writes no Newtonsoft setting (M21.D1).

promises.page: An app that registers Fusion at startup, whose own preview endpoint returns a resident written by JsonConvert.SerializeObject with no settings of the app's, and a Preview button that loads the endpoint's text into a preview element.
promises.opposite: The same endpoint written under the app's own camel-case JsonSerializerSettings shows {"residentId":7,"givenName":"Rose"}: the app's settings decide.
promises.defect: Registering Fusion sets Newtonsoft's process-wide default to camel case, so the app's own call writes residentId and givenName although the app chose nothing.

verdicts.reason: A vendor named by a string the runtime picks a driver by, native or fusion (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/browser-objects/component-driver.ts:89-90 at 623dd4a27), so the runtime names each vendor it serves. The rewrite carries the vendor as data the one driver follows (D17.3): the ComponentVendor a declaration names (M12.N1).

features.summary: FusionGrid: one declaration of the Syncfusion Grid by its JavaScript names, its data, paging, sorting, filtering, searching, grouping, columns, selection, editing, exports and print, each EJ2 33.1.47's public member; the payloads of its ten events; the render helper that renders it with an element id the view gives and a plan; the column field names, edit templates and edit dialog it writes; and the column rules it gives the grid from the validator. Main spreads the slice over twenty-two files whose calls name members by strings over ComponentRef, payload classes with setters, extensions that take the pipeline, a builder of its own and a Reactive extension on it; the redesign declares it in five files, the shape the rewrite keeps, with its exports awaited, its enums written as EJ2 reads them, its rows named as every framework read names them (M21.D1), and every column rule either checked by the column's editor or refused where the view renders.

sentences.text: public Property<IEnumerable<TRow>> Rows<TRow>() where TRow : class => Property<IEnumerable<TRow>>("dataSource");
public Property<IFusionGridPage<TRow>> Page<TRow>() where TRow : class => Property<IFusionGridPage<TRow>>("dataSource");
public void ShowColumn(Field key) => Method(key, Fixed("field"), name: "showColumns");
public void AddRecordAt<TRow>(Arg<TRow> data, Arg<int> index) where TRow : class => Method(data, index, name: "addRecord");
public static BrowserRule Email(string message) => new PatternRule(EmailPattern, "", message, Condition.Always);

FusionGrid declares the EJ2 Grid by its JavaScript names: dataSource as Rows<TRow>() or Page<TRow>(), the result and count of a remote page; its paging, sorting, filtering, searching and grouping; its columns' showColumns, hideColumns, autoFitColumns, reorderColumns and getColumnByField; its selection; its editing, addRecord with and without an index, updateRow, setRowData, setCellValue, editCell, updateCell, saveCell and getBatchChanges; refresh, refreshHeader, openColumnChooser and print; each EJ2 33.1.47's public member.

ExcelExport, CsvExport and PdfExport are declared MethodAsync, as grid.d.ts declares each to return a promise, so a step after an export runs once its file is written and a failed export stops its pipeline (D11.3, B15).

DataStateChange, ToolbarClick, RecordClick<TRow>(), RowSelected<TRow>(), ActionBegin<TRow>(), ActionComplete<TRow>(), BeginEdit<TRow>(), CellSave<TRow, TValue>(), CellSaved<TRow, TValue>() and BeforeBatchSave<TRow>() hand payloads read with Read, each payload's cancel its Property<bool>; a payload declares a name only where EJ2's type does, recordClick's and toolbarClick's, so dataStateChange's, its action's, rowSelected's, actionBegin's and actionComplete's declare none.

FusionGridSortDirection and FusionGridTextFilterOperator carry System.Text.Json's string enum converter, so the live form writes Ascending and contains as sortColumn's SortDirection and filterByColumn's operator take them (D7.7).

Html.FusionGrid(plan, id, rows, build => ..) renders the grid with the rows the view hands it, written by M21.D1, and FusionGridColumns.Of<TRow>().Field(r => r.Member) names a column's field as every framework read names it.
The rendered grid's Reactive(g => g.RecordClick<TRow>(), pipeline) and its other events handle the grid from the plan's start, and pipeline.Component<FusionGrid>(id) reaches it from any block.

FusionGridValidation.From<TRow>(rules).Field(r => r.Member) gives a column the validator's rules its editor checks, each in the validator's own form, and refuses where the view renders a rule the editor cannot check that is not the server's (M21.X203).
FusionGridEditTemplates.Select, DateInput and DialogForm write a column's editor and an edit dialog, each select opening at the row's value.

features.oracle: Syncfusion EJ2 33.1.47's Grid as its TypeScript declares it (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts, its event payloads in src/grid/base/interface.d.ts, SortDirection in src/grid/base/enum.d.ts, the toolbar's ClickEventArgs in @syncfusion/ej2-navigations, a column's rules as @syncfusion/ej2-inputs' FormValidator reads them), each JavaScript name read there by the lead and checked by scratchpad m21/tools/dts.py, whose name: overrides (showColumns, hideColumns, autoFitColumns, addRecord) and generic payloads were read by hand; the Syncfusion.EJ2.AspNet.Core 33.1.47 builder as spec/probes/AspNetCoreBinding/FusionProbes.cs renders it; and the browser, by the promises.

defects.defect: Main calls the grid's excelExport, csvExport and pdfExport as plain calls (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridToolingExtensions.cs:38-59 at 623dd4a27) and the redesign declares them Method() (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:207-213 at 65fdf118d), while each returns a promise (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts:3849, :3859, :3870): the step after an export runs before its file is written, and a failed export goes unseen. The rewrite declares them MethodAsync (D11.3, B15).

Both lines declare a name EJ2's types do not: on dataStateChange's payload (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/Events/FusionGridOnDataStateChange.cs:18 at 623dd4a27, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:326 at 65fdf118d; @syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/interface.d.ts:2479-2508), on its action (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/Events/FusionGridOnDataStateChange.cs:131 at 623dd4a27, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:452 at 65fdf118d; @syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/interface.d.ts:2495), on rowSelected's (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/Events/FusionGridOnRowSelected.cs:23 at 623dd4a27, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:546 at 65fdf118d; @syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/interface.d.ts:1374-1402) and on actionBegin's and actionComplete's (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/Events/FusionGridOnEditing.cs:27 at 623dd4a27, Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:588 at 65fdf118d; @syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/grid.d.ts:1790, :1796). EJ2's observer stamps one at run time (@syncfusion/ej2-base/src/observer.js:92), which no contract declares. The vendor contract analyzer (N17.2) refuses each by ALIS016, and the rewrite's payloads declare no name where EJ2's type declares none; recordClick's and toolbarClick's keep theirs (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/interface.d.ts:1438).

A rule a grid column's editor cannot check is dropped where the view renders with nothing said: a rule under a condition (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridValidation.cs:96 at 623dd4a27, :112 at 65fdf118d); a rule EJ2's column validator has no key for, as GreaterThan or a comparison with another member (:104-138 at 623dd4a27, :120-144 at 65fdf118d); and one of two patterns on one column (:119-121 at 623dd4a27, where the second replaces the first, and :132 at 65fdf118d, which keeps the first). The column saves a value its validator refuses, and only the server's answer says so. The rewrite refuses it where the view renders: "'{member}' has a rule the grid column's editor cannot check ({rule}); check it on the server with ServerOnly(), or give the column a rule its editor checks."

Main's select editors open at their first option: the column template's Select and the edit dialog's Select write no selected option (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridEditTemplates.cs:88-95 and :146-151 at 623dd4a27), so a row whose status is Discharged opens its editor at Admitted, and saving it unchanged writes Admitted. The redesign selects the row's value (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridEditTemplates.cs:111, :121-122, :192 at 65fdf118d), which the rewrite keeps.

Main gives an email or url column EJ2's own email and url rules (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridValidation.cs:108-110 at 623dd4a27), whose patterns need a dotted domain (@syncfusion/ej2-inputs/src/form-validator/form-validator.js:29-32), so an inline edit refuses rose@ward and http://intranet/residents, which the server's EmailAddress and Url accept. The rewrite writes the validator's own patterns as the column's regex, as the redesign does (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Validation/BrowserRule.cs:62, :69 at 65fdf118d).

A column bound to a member that carries [JsonPropertyName("room")] shows empty cells for rows handed over with the view: a column's field names the member by System.Text.Json (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridColumns.cs:37 at 65fdf118d) while EJ2 writes the builder's DataSource through Newtonsoft as roomNumber (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-newtonsoft-defaults). The rewrite's render helper hands the rows by M21.D1 (probe:fusion-ej2-builder-raw-json).

The redesign's FusionGridSortDirection and FusionGridTextFilterOperator carry no string converter (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGrid.cs:270, :280 at 65fdf118d), and a JsonStringEnumMemberName holds only under one, so in the live form (D7.7) sortColumn receives 0 where SortDirection is 'Ascending' | 'Descending' (@syncfusion/ej2-grids/src/grid/base/enum.d.ts:40). The vendor contract analyzer's type check (N17.2) refuses an enum against the vendor's literal union by ALIS037 (X17.46), and the rewrite's enums carry System.Text.Json's string enum converter. Main writes both as text by hand (Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionGrid/FusionGridQueryExtensions.cs:153-164 at 623dd4a27).

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to Excel button sets the status to Exporting, runs ExcelExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The Excel file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to CSV button sets the status to Exporting, runs CsvExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The CSV file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Export to PDF button sets the status to Exporting, runs PdfExport, then sets the status to Exported.
promises.outcome: The PDF file's download starts while the status reads Exporting, and the status reads Exported after it.
promises.opposite: Before the click, no download starts and the status reads Ready.
promises.defect: The status reads Exported before the download starts, since the export's promise is dropped.

promises.page: A ward grid whose Beds column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Beds rule is GreaterThan(0) When(r => r.IsOpen).
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Beds and its conditional rule.
promises.opposite: The same rule with no condition renders, and editing Beds to 0 shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: The conditional rule is dropped, the page renders, and a row saves 0 beds with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A ward grid whose Beds column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Beds rule is GreaterThan(0).
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Beds and GreaterThan.
promises.opposite: With GreaterThanOrEqualTo(1) the page renders, and editing Beds to 0 shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: GreaterThan has no column key and is dropped, so a row saves 0 beds with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A contacts grid whose Email column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Email rules are Matches("^[a-z.]+@") and Matches("@care\\.org$").
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with M21.X203's message, naming Email and its second pattern.
promises.opposite: With Matches("@care\\.org$") alone the page renders, and editing Email to rose@ward.com shows its message under the cell.
promises.defect: One pattern is dropped and the page renders, so a row saves an address only the dropped pattern refuses (rose@ward.com, or Rose@care.org) with no message until the server answers.

promises.page: A residents grid whose Status column edits with FusionGridEditTemplates.Select over Admitted, Discharged and On leave, and a row whose status is Discharged.
promises.gesture: Double-click the Discharged row's Status cell.
promises.opposite: On a row whose status is On leave, the select shows On leave.
promises.defect: The select opens at its first option, Admitted, and saving the row unchanged writes Admitted.

promises.page: A residents grid that edits in a dialog written by FusionGridEditTemplates.DialogForm with a Status select over Admitted, Discharged and On leave, and a row whose status is Discharged.
promises.gesture: Select the Discharged row and click Edit.
promises.outcome: The dialog's Status select shows Discharged.
promises.opposite: On a row whose status is On leave, the dialog's select shows On leave.
promises.defect: The dialog's select opens at Admitted, and saving the dialog unchanged writes Admitted.

promises.page: A contacts grid whose Email column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Email rule is EmailAddress().
promises.gesture: Double-click a row's Email cell, type rose@ward and press Enter.
promises.outcome: The row saves rose@ward, as the server's EmailAddress accepts it.
promises.opposite: Typing rose and pressing Enter shows the email message under the cell.
promises.defect: EJ2's own email pattern needs a dotted domain, so rose@ward shows the email message and the row does not save.

promises.page: A links grid whose Address column takes FusionGridValidation's rules for a validator whose Address rule is Url().
promises.gesture: Double-click a row's Address cell, type http://intranet/residents and press Enter.
promises.outcome: The row saves http://intranet/residents, as the server's Url accepts it.
promises.opposite: Typing intranet/residents and pressing Enter shows the url message under the cell.
promises.defect: EJ2's own url pattern needs a dotted domain, so http://intranet/residents shows the url message and the row does not save.

promises.page: A beds grid rendered by Html.FusionGrid(plan, "beds", rows, build => ..) with the rows East 1 and East 2, of a bed class whose room member carries [JsonPropertyName("room")], and a Room column whose field is FusionGridColumns.Of<Bed>().Field(b => b.RoomNumber).
promises.outcome: The Room column shows East 1 and East 2.
promises.opposite: A Ward column bound to a member with no JsonPropertyName shows the ward of each row too.
promises.defect: EJ2 writes the handed rows through Newtonsoft as roomNumber while the column names room, so the Room column shows two empty cells.
